items.description: In April 1961, surgeon Leonid Rogozov found himself in a dire situation in Antarctica when he developed acute appendicitis. Stranded at a remote Soviet research station, he realized that evacuation was impossible. Demonstrating extraordinary resolve, he performed surgery on himself with local anesthesia, assisted by two colleagues, successfully removing his appendix. This incredible act is celebrated as a significant milestone in the annals of remote medical practice.

items.description: At an age when many people slow down, Kamla Negi started a new life, new job and took on one of the toughest jobs in the hills of Uttarakhand. She is 60-years-old and is repairing punctures in scooters and cars. Not only this, she is also handling the massive tyres of trucks, dumpers, buses and JCB machines. The woman belongs from Nainital's Ramgarh region and has built a reputation for doing work traditionally associated with men.

items.title: Rupee climbs to near 7-month high of 93.69 against dollar
items.description: On Wednesday, the Indian rupee surged to a close seven-month peak of 93.69 against the US dollar, fueled by a dip in oil prices and a surge in foreign capital into Indian stocks. Although exporters are evaluating hedging options, their engagement is lackluster due to recent regulations. As Brent crude oil prices settle around $92 per barrel, experts forecast the rupee to oscillate within the bandwidth of 93.25 to 94.

items.title: Chased & then shot: Chilling CCTV video of ex-Tech Mahindra regional head's murder
items.author: NIKHIL SHARMA
items.description: CCTV footage captured the events leading to the murder of Paramjeet Dhankhar by his neighbour, Mohan Sharma. An argument lasting four minutes escalated, resulting in Sharma shooting Dhankhar multiple times. Despite attempts to escape, Dhankhar was pursued and fired upon even after collapsing. Investigations indicate a long-standing dispute over parking may have sparked the incident. Sharma was later arrested, with police probing previous disagreements that might have contributed.

items.title: Ladakh protest row: Police remove Sonam Wangchuk from protest site
items.author: NASEER GANAI
items.description: Ladakh Police removed climate activist Sonam Wangchuk from a protest site in Leh on Wednesday evening. Wangchuk and local leaders protested against hill council elections set for December 4 due to harsh winter conditions. They argued that approximately 25% of Ladakhis are away from the region during this period. The local administration imposed a ban on protests to maintain public order during the elections.

items.title: Mutual funds kept selling stakes in 79 companies for 4 quarters
items.description: Mutual funds in India have continued supporting domestic equities despite market volatility and foreign selling. They decreased stakes in 79 companies for four consecutive quarters until September 2026. While domestic investments by mutual funds totaled ₹4.6 lakh crore, foreign portfolio investors sold about $26 billion in equities. Notable companies with reduced mutual fund stakes include Shivalik Bimetal Controls and TeamLease Services, among others.

items.title: Hindalco's value-add focus to drive growth and a stock re-rating
items.description: Hindalco reported record revenue and profit in the latest quarter amid increasing metal prices and improved Novelis performance. The company anticipates muted growth due to declining aluminium prices and elevated input costs. It has initiated significant investments in capacity expansion and enhancing value-added products. Novelis expects to transition towards increased earnings and cost savings in the coming years. Hindalco's strategic moves aim to fortify its position in the aluminium market.

items.title: Sensex, Nifty hit 8-month highs as banks, auto stocks rally
items.description: Indian equities have seen significant gains recently, with the Sensex and Nifty reaching their highest levels since February. Heavyweight stocks in the banking and auto sectors contributed to this rally amid declining crude oil prices. Profit booking was expected as investors took some money off the table after the sharp market movements. Foreign investors purchased nearly $7 billion worth of Indian equities during this period.

items.author: etimes.in
items.description: Nitesh Tiwari's film 'Ramayana: Rise of a Legend' has achieved significant box office success within its first week. The film, featuring Ranbir Kapoor and Yash, is close to reaching Rs 1,000 crores worldwide. It collected Rs 934.55 crores globally, with substantial earnings from both domestic and international markets. The Hindi version has dominated the Indian revenue, contributing to a total of Rs 394 crores.

items.title: Indians buy 30% more gold after recent price correction
items.description: Indians showed a significant increase in gold and silver purchases during Dhanteras-Diwali this year. Gold buying rose by 30% while silver demand increased by 10% compared to last year. Consumers bought 52 tonnes of gold valued at ₹72,000 crore and 300 tonnes of silver worth ₹5,400 crore. The rise in purchases was fueled by lower prices and upcoming wedding season. Jewellers expressed optimism about continued consumer interest in precious metals.

items.title: Debt Mutual Funds: What investors should know before investing
items.description: Debt mutual funds faced substantial outflows amounting to Rs 1.8 lakh crore in September, which was considerable. These outflows were primarily due to liquidity needs, particularly among companies and institutional investors. Investors should evaluate their investment horizon and risk tolerance before choosing a suitable debt fund. Despite the outflows, debt funds remain important for managing short-term financial goals and diversifying portfolios.

items.title: Equity mutual fund inflows fall 14% in October as investors trim smallcap exposure
items.description: Inflows into equity mutual fund schemes fell by 14% in October, reflecting a trend of reduced investor allocations. Although smallcap funds saw decreasing inflows, large and midcap funds experienced significant increases in investments. Systematic investment plan contributions also declined slightly, while the stoppage ratio rose notably during the same period. In contrast, debt mutual funds attracted substantial inflows after previous outflows, with liquid funds leading this rebound.

items.title: Rare right whale calf spotted with 38-year-old mother; season total rises to 24
items.author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
items.description: In a remarkable development, scientists have confirmed the sighting of a previously unrecorded North Atlantic right whale calf near Quebec, bringing this season's total to 24, the highest since 2009. Researchers believe the calf's mother, Silt, gave birth in the warmer waters of the southeastern U.S. Despite this positive news, the North Atlantic right whale population remains critically endangered, with an estimated 380 individuals.

items.title: SC: Indians married here can't get divorced abroad
items.author: AMIT ANAND CHOUDHARY
items.description: In a landmark decision, the Supreme Court declared that divorces executed overseas, based on grounds not acknowledged under Indian law, are invalid. items.title: Psychology says constant scrolling before work may be a form of avoidance
items.author: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK
items.description: Procrastination often stems from evading unpleasant emotions tied to challenging tasks. People are naturally drawn to immediate pleasures rather than the long-term rewards of accomplishing their responsibilities. Studies show that while distractions such as social media offer a quick escape, they often lead to feelings of guilt. Techniques like dividing tasks into manageable parts and scheduling specific times for leisure can effectively combat procrastination.

items.title: Delhi's traffic curbs in vain? Report suggests they may have made little difference
items.author: PRIYANGI AGARWAL
items.description: Delhi’s air pollution levels have increased this year compared to 2025, with stubble smoke adding to the problem. Emergency traffic measures put in place have not reduced congestion significantly, impacting daily travel times. Traffic analysis indicates that local vehicular emissions play a major role in air quality issues. NO2 levels have surged recently during evening traffic hours, remaining high despite road traffic decreasing.

items.title: Amanda Seyfried on deciding when her children can watch her own movies
items.author: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK
items.description: Amanda Seyfried opened up about her daughter's honest reactions to her films, particularly 'Mean Girls'. While Nina appreciated Seyfried's acting, she found the film lacking in humor. Having also seen 'Mamma Mia!', she recognized her mother's musical talent. Seyfried plans to share her upcoming film 'Steps', which explores complex relationships, showcasing the unique viewpoints children have of their celebrity parents and how those views evolve over time.
